## Graph container

### `KnowledgeGraph`

```
KnowledgeGraph(; base = BNR, prefixes = Dict())
```

A collection of BioNExt resources keyed by identifier, kept in insertion order.

Identifiers are plain strings: a bare local name (`"TP53"`, minted under `base`), a CURIE (`"UniProt:P04637"`, expanded with `prefixes` or identifiers.org), or a full IRI.

Queries scan the graph unless it is indexed; see `index!`.

### `add!`

```
add!(kg, resources...; replace = false) -> kg
```

Add resources. Adding an id that already exists throws unless `replace = true`.

### `resources`

```
resources(kg, T = Resource) -> Vector{T}
```

All resources of type `T` (abstract types allowed), e.g. `resources(kg, NodeEntity)`.

### `nodes`

```
nodes(kg) -> Vector{NodeEntity}
```

All node entities, in insertion order.

### `edges`

```
edges(kg) -> Vector{EdgeEntity}
```

All edge entities (interactions, influences, reactions), in insertion order.

### `pathways`

```
pathways(kg) -> Vector{PathwayModule}
```

### `references`

```
references(kg, x) -> Vector{Pair{String,Symbol}}
```

Every `(resource id => field)` that refers to `x`; useful before deleting it.

### `referrers`

```
referrers(kg, x) -> Vector{Pair{String,Symbol}}
```

Every `(resource id => field)` whose reference field contains `x`, in insertion order. Uses the index when there is one.


## Queries

### `edges_of`

```
edges_of(kg, x; side = :any, type = nothing) -> Vector{EdgeEntity}
```

Edges in which `x` (id or resource) participates — the `bn:participatesInEdge` view. `side` is `:left`, `:right` or `:any`; `type` optionally restricts to edges whose relationship type `is_a` the given term.

### `neighbors`

```
neighbors(kg, x; direction = :both, type = nothing) -> Vector{String}
```

Ids connected to `x` through edges. `:out` follows left→right, `:in` right→left.

### `pathways_of`

```
pathways_of(kg, x) -> Vector{PathwayModule}
```

Pathways listing `x` as a component (`bn:participatesInPathway`).

### `components`

```
components(kg, pathway; recursive = false) -> Vector{String}
```

Component ids of a pathway; with `recursive = true`, sub-pathways are expanded too.

### `complexes_of`

```
complexes_of(kg, x) -> Vector{MolecularComplex}
```

Complexes having `x` as a subunit (`bn:memberOfComplex`).

### `variants`

```
variants(kg, x) -> Vector{NodeEntity}
```

Resources declared `isVariantOf` `x` (`bn:hasVariant`).

### `ortholog_groups_of`

```
ortholog_groups_of(kg, x) -> Vector{OrthologGroup}
```


## Indexing

### `index!`

```
index!(kg) -> kg
```

Build a reverse index of all references and keep it up to date. Afterwards, `edges_of`, `neighbors`, `pathways_of`, `complexes_of`, `variants`, `ortholog_groups_of` and `references` look up the index instead of scanning the whole graph.

`add!`, `delete!`, `merge!`, `load!`, `resolve!` and `integrate!` keep the index current. Editing reference fields directly (e.g. `push!(kg["e1"].right, "x")`) does **not**: call `reindex!(kg)` after such edits. Results are verified against the current fields, so a stale index can miss new references but never reports removed ones.

### `reindex!`

```
reindex!(kg) -> kg
```

Rebuild the index after editing reference fields directly. Does nothing if `kg` is not indexed.

### `unindex!`

```
unindex!(kg) -> kg
```

Drop the index; queries scan again.

### `isindexed`

```
isindexed(kg) -> Bool
```


## Graph algorithms

### `degree_of`

```
degree_of(kg, x; direction = :both, type = nothing) -> Int
```

Number of edges `x` takes part in. `direction = :out` counts edges where `x` is on the left, `:in` where it is on the right; `type` restricts to a relationship type and its subtypes.

### `shortest_path`

```
shortest_path(kg, from, to; direction = :out, type = nothing, reify = false,
              max_hops = typemax(Int)) -> Union{Vector{String}, Nothing}
```

Fewest-hop path of ids from `from` to `to`, or `nothing` if there is none. It follows the same arcs as `network(kg; reify, type)` (and so `to_graph`): left → right for `direction = :out`, right → left for `:in`, either way for `:both`.

With `reify = false`, each step goes from a participant to a participant of the same edge; an edge that is itself a participant (the target of an `Influence`) is an end point. With `reify = true`, edges are steps of their own (`A → e1 → B`), so a path can run through an influence on an edge to that edge's participants.

### `network_components`

```
network_components(kg; type = nothing, reify = false) -> Vector{Vector{String}}
```

Weakly connected components (ignoring direction) of `network(kg; reify, type)`, largest first, each in insertion order. Every node entity is in exactly one component (isolated nodes as singletons), as is every id that occurs as an edge participant. With `reify = true`, every edge is a member too and is joined to its participants, so an influence on an edge connects its source to that edge's participants.

### `subgraph`

```
subgraph(kg, seeds; hops = 0, type = nothing, include_context = true) -> KnowledgeGraph
```

A new graph containing copies of `seeds` and everything within `hops` edge steps of them. Each step adds the edges of the current ids and all their participants. With `include_context = true`, resources the kept ones refer to without being part of the network (taxa, provenance, cofactors, complex subunits, ...) are copied as well, so the result validates without dangling-reference warnings for them. Pathways are kept only if they are seeds; their `components` are trimmed to what was kept.

### `to_graph`

```
to_graph(kg; reify = false, directed = true, type = nothing)
```julia
-> (graph, ids::Vector{String}, vertex::Dict{String,Int})
```
```

Convert to a Graphs.jl graph so its algorithms (centrality, communities, flows, ...) can run on the network. Requires `using Graphs` (or `import Graphs`), which loads the package extension. Vertices are the nodes of `network(kg; reify)`: vertex `i` is `ids[i]`, and `vertex[id]` is the reverse lookup. `type` keeps only edges of that relationship type (and its subtypes). The graph is a `SimpleDiGraph`, or a `SimpleGraph` with `directed = false`; parallel arcs collapse into one.


## Entity resolution

### `duplicates`

```
duplicates(kg; use_xrefs = false, prefix_aliases = Dict()) -> Vector{Vector{String}}
```

Groups of resource ids that describe the same entity: same class and at least one shared identifier (id or external id, transitively). Only groups of two or more are returned, each in insertion order.

### `resolve!`

```
resolve!(kg; prefer = String[], merge_edges = true, use_xrefs = false,
         prefix_aliases = Dict(), on_conflict = keep_first) -> Resolution
```

Merge every group found by `duplicates` into one canonical resource, then rewrite all references in the graph to the canonical ids.

  * **Canonical id**: the member whose id prefix comes first in `prefer` (e.g. `["UniProt", "HGNC", "Ensembl"]`, case-insensitive), else the earliest added. `prefer` may also be a function `group -> id`.
  * **Fields**: vector fields are united; empty single-valued fields are filled in; differing values are settled by `on_conflict(field, kept, other)` (default: keep the canonical's value) and recorded as `Conflict`s.
  * **Traceability**: merged ids are added to the canonical resource's `external_ids`, so `find_entity(kg, old_id)` still works.
  * **Edges**: with `merge_edges = true`, edges that become identical (same class, type, and participant sets) are merged too, repeatedly, since merging edges can make edges that target them identical.

### `integrate!`

```
integrate!(kg, other; kwargs...) -> Resolution
```

Bring the resources of `other` (e.g. a graph loaded from another database) into `kg` and resolve duplicates. Resources of `other` are copied; one with an id already in `kg` is merged field by field into the existing one (same class required). Then `resolve!` runs with `kwargs`, merging entities linked through `external_ids`. `other` is not modified.

### `find_entity`

```
find_entity(kg, identifier; use_xrefs = false, prefix_aliases = Dict()) -> Union{Resource,Nothing}
```

The resource whose id or `external_ids` match `identifier` (after normalization), e.g. `find_entity(kg, "Ensembl:ENSP00000269305")` finds the protein stored as `UniProt:P04637` if that Ensembl id is among its external ids. Returns the first match.

### `identifier_map`

```
identifier_map(kg; use_xrefs = false, prefix_aliases = Dict()) -> Dict{String,String}
```

Normalized identifier ⇒ resource id, covering every id and external id. Build it once for many lookups; `find_entity` does a single lookup.

### `normalize_identifier`

```
normalize_identifier(kg, id; prefix_aliases = Dict()) -> String
```

Canonical comparison key for an identifier: its full IRI, with the identifiers.org prefix lower-cased and renamed through `prefix_aliases` (e.g. `Dict("uniprotkb" => "uniprot")`), so `"UniProt:P04637"`, `"uniprot:P04637"` and `"https://identifiers.org/UniProt:P04637"` match.

### `Resolution`

```
Resolution
```

Result of `resolve!` / `integrate!`:

  * `mapping`: merged id ⇒ canonical id (canonical ids are not keys)
  * `groups`: each merged group, canonical id first
  * `conflicts`: single-valued fields whose values disagreed

### `Conflict`

```
Conflict(id, field, kept, discarded, source)
```

Two merged resources had different values for a single-valued field. `kept` is the value the canonical resource `id` ended up with; `discarded` came from (or stayed with) `source`.

### `keep_first`

No documentation found.

`BioNExt.keep_first` is a `Function`.

## Validation

### `validate`

```
validate(kg) -> Vector{Issue}
```

Check the graph against the BioNExt ontology:

  * reference ranges (`rdfs:range` and `owl:allValuesFrom` restrictions, e.g. a `Reaction`'s right side must be NodeEntities; variants must be of the same class)
  * controlled-vocabulary membership (relationship types, cellular locations, regions)
  * `bn:expectedLeft` / `bn:expectedRight` of each edge's relationship type
  * edges need a left and a right participant; variants need exactly one HGVS string
  * positive integer coordinates
  * dangling references (warning)

### `Issue`

```
Issue(severity, id, message)
```

A validation finding. `severity` is `:error` (violates the ontology) or `:warning` (e.g. a reference to an id not present in the graph).


## Data quality

### `audit`

```
audit(kg; checks = all, skip = Symbol[], max_per_check = 1000, patterns = ID_PATTERNS) -> AuditReport
```

Check the data in `kg` for problems the ontology rules cannot see (see `AUDIT_CHECKS`):

|                 Check |                                                                                      Looks for |     Severities |
| ---------------------:| ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------:| --------------:|
|           `:ontology` |                                                                  everything `validate` reports | error, warning |
|        `:identifiers` |                             ids and cross-references that do not match their database's format |        warning |
|          `:sequences` |                             invalid residues for the molecule type; `length` ≠ sequence length | error, warning |
|        `:coordinates` |                                         end before start; length inconsistent with coordinates | error, warning |
| `:modification_sites` |                                            sites beyond the sequence or on a different residue | error, warning |
|             `:values` |                  NaN/Inf scores, confidence outside [0,1], malformed InChIKey/CAS/formula/HGVS | error, warning |
|         `:duplicates` |                                          entities that `resolve!` would merge; identical edges |        warning |
|              `:edges` | self-loops, cross-species edges, activating and inhibiting edges between the same participants |           info |
|          `:structure` |                                   empty complexes/pathways/ortholog groups; containment cycles |  warning, info |
|       `:connectivity` |                                             isolated nodes; unused taxa and provenance records |           info |
|         `:annotation` |                        entities without name, organism, provenance; edges without publications |           info |

`checks` selects checks, `skip` leaves some out. At most `max_per_check` findings are kept per check; `counts` always has the full numbers.

### `AuditReport`

```
AuditReport
```

Result of `audit`: `findings` (at most `max_per_check` per check), `counts` (all findings, by check and severity, including those not kept) and `checks` (the checks that ran). Use `findings(report; check, severity)`, `passed(report)` and `show`.

### `Finding`

```
Finding(check, severity, id, message)
```

One audit result. `severity` is `:error` (the data are wrong), `:warning` (probably wrong or needs attention) or `:info` (worth knowing, often fine).

### `AUDIT_CHECKS`

```
Array{T,N} <: AbstractArray{T,N}
```

`N`-dimensional dense array with elements of type `T`.

```
Array{T}(undef, dims)
Array{T,N}(undef, dims)
```

Construct an uninitialized `N`-dimensional [`Array`](@ref) containing elements of type `T`. `N` can either be supplied explicitly, as in `Array{T,N}(undef, dims)`, or be determined by the length or number of `dims`. `dims` may be a tuple or a series of integer arguments corresponding to the lengths in each dimension. If the rank `N` is supplied explicitly, then it must match the length or number of `dims`. Here [`undef`](@ref) is the [`UndefInitializer`](@ref).

# Examples

```julia-repl
julia> A = Array{Float64, 2}(undef, 2, 3) # N given explicitly
2×3 Matrix{Float64}:
 6.90198e-310  6.90198e-310  6.90198e-310
 6.90198e-310  6.90198e-310  0.0

julia> B = Array{Float64}(undef, 4) # N determined by the input
4-element Vector{Float64}:
   2.360075077e-314
 NaN
   2.2671131793e-314
   2.299821756e-314

julia> similar(B, 2, 4, 1) # use typeof(B), and the given size
2×4×1 Array{Float64, 3}:
[:, :, 1] =
 2.26703e-314  2.26708e-314  0.0           2.80997e-314
 0.0           2.26703e-314  2.26708e-314  0.0
```

```
Array{T}(nothing, dims)
Array{T,N}(nothing, dims)
```

Construct an `N`-dimensional [`Array`](@ref) containing elements of type `T`, initialized with [`nothing`](@ref) entries. Element type `T` must be able to hold these values, i.e. `Nothing <: T`.

# Examples

```jldoctest
julia> Array{Union{Nothing, String}}(nothing, 2)
2-element Vector{Union{Nothing, String}}:
 nothing
 nothing

julia> Array{Union{Nothing, Int}}(nothing, 2, 3)
2×3 Matrix{Union{Nothing, Int64}}:
 nothing  nothing  nothing
 nothing  nothing  nothing
```

```
Array{T}(missing, dims)
Array{T,N}(missing, dims)
```

Construct an `N`-dimensional [`Array`](@ref) containing elements of type `T`, initialized with [`missing`](@ref) entries. Element type `T` must be able to hold these values, i.e. `Missing <: T`.

# Examples

```jldoctest
julia> Array{Union{Missing, String}}(missing, 2)
2-element Vector{Union{Missing, String}}:
 missing
 missing

julia> Array{Union{Missing, Int}}(missing, 2, 3)
2×3 Matrix{Union{Missing, Int64}}:
 missing  missing  missing
 missing  missing  missing
```

### `ID_PATTERNS`

```
Dict([itr])
```

`Dict{K,V}()` constructs a hash table with keys of type `K` and values of type `V`. Keys are compared with [`isequal`](@ref) and hashed with [`hash`](@ref).

Given a single iterable argument, constructs a [`Dict`](@ref) whose key-value pairs are taken from 2-tuples `(key,value)` generated by the argument.

# Examples

```jldoctest
julia> Dict([("A", 1), ("B", 2)])
Dict{String, Int64} with 2 entries:
  "B" => 2
  "A" => 1
```

Alternatively, a sequence of pair arguments may be passed.

```jldoctest
julia> Dict("A"=>1, "B"=>2)
Dict{String, Int64} with 2 entries:
  "B" => 2
  "A" => 1
```

### `findings`

```
findings(report; check = nothing, severity = nothing) -> Vector{Finding}
```

### `passed`

```
passed(report; fail_on = :error) -> Bool
```

`true` when the report has no findings of severity `fail_on` or worse (`:error`; `:warning` = errors or warnings; `:info` = anything).

### `count_findings`

```
count_findings(report; check = nothing, severity = nothing) -> Int
```

Number of findings (including those not kept because of `max_per_check`).

### `assert_quality`

```
assert_quality(kg; fail_on = :error, kwargs...) -> AuditReport
```

Run `audit` (with `kwargs`) and throw a `QualityError` showing the report if it does not pass at level `fail_on`; otherwise return the report. Use it as a gate in pipelines and tests.

## Statistics

### `graph_stats`

```
graph_stats(kg; top = 10, clustering = :auto) -> GraphStats
```

Collect statistics of `kg` (see `GraphStats` for every field). `top` is the number of hubs listed. The clustering coefficient is computed when `clustering = true`, or with `:auto` when the graph has at most 200,000 nodes. Display the result for a report, or turn it into rows with `stats_table` and save it with `write_stats`.

### `GraphStats`

```
GraphStats
```

Statistics of a knowledge graph, computed by `graph_stats`. Fields:

  * `resources`, `classes` (class ⇒ count), `relationship_types` (type ⇒ count)
  * `nodes`, `edges`, `isolated` (nodes in no edge)
  * `degree`, `in_degree`, `out_degree`: `(min, max, mean, median)` over nodes; a node's degree is the number of edges it takes part in (`degree_of`); in = as a target (right), out = as a source (left)
  * `degree_distribution` (degree ⇒ number of nodes), `hubs` (id ⇒ degree, highest first)
  * `components`, `largest_component`, `largest_fraction`: weakly connected components of the flattened network (`network_components`)
  * `arcs` (distinct directed pairs in `network(kg)`), `density`, `reciprocity` (fraction of arcs whose reverse also exists), `self_loops`, `clustering` (mean local clustering coefficient over nodes with ≥ 2 neighbours, undirected; `nothing` if not computed)
  * `pathways` and `complexes`: `(count, mean, max)` of their direct components / subunits; `pathway_depth`: deepest nesting of sub-pathways
  * `organisms` (taxon ⇒ entities), `locations` (term ⇒ nodes), `id_prefixes` (prefix ⇒ resources)
  * `sources` (provenance ⇒ entities), `multi_source` (entities with ≥ 2 provenance records), `source_overlap` ((a, b) ⇒ entities shared by both)
  * `publications` (distinct references), `completeness` (annotation ⇒ fraction of applicable resources)

### `stats_table`

```
stats_table(s::GraphStats) -> Vector{NamedTuple{(:section, :metric, :value)}}
```

The statistics as rows, for printing, saving (`write_stats`) or a DataFrame.

### `write_stats`

```
write_stats(io_or_path, s::GraphStats; format = :markdown)
```

Save statistics as a Markdown report (`:markdown`, `.md`), a table (`:tsv`, `.tsv`; `:csv`, `.csv`) or JSON (`:json`, `.json`). With a path, the format follows the extension.


## Vocabulary

### `Term`

```
Term
```

A controlled-vocabulary term of the BioNExt ontology (a subclass of `bn:ControlledVocabulary`, e.g. a relationship type, cellular component or region type). `expected_left`/`expected_right` hold the `bn:expectedLeft`/`bn:expectedRight` annotations of relationship types (empty = unconstrained).

### `term`

```
term(id::Symbol) -> Term
```

Look up a controlled-vocabulary term, e.g. `term(:Phosphorylation)`.

### `terms`

```
terms(root::Symbol) -> Vector{Symbol}
```

All terms below `root` (excluding `root` itself), sorted, e.g. `terms(:RelationshipType)`.

### `is_a`

```
is_a(id::Symbol, ancestor::Symbol) -> Bool
```

True if term `id` equals `ancestor` or is a (transitive) subclass of it.

### `is_term`

```
is_term(id::Symbol) -> Bool
```

### `VOCABULARY`

```
Dict([itr])
```

`Dict{K,V}()` constructs a hash table with keys of type `K` and values of type `V`. Keys are compared with [`isequal`](@ref) and hashed with [`hash`](@ref).

Given a single iterable argument, constructs a [`Dict`](@ref) whose key-value pairs are taken from 2-tuples `(key,value)` generated by the argument.

## Types and schema

### `Resource`

Supertype of everything a `KnowledgeGraph` stores: entities and provenance records.

### `Entity`

Abstract `bn:Entity`: any biological or conceptual entity (nodes, edges, pathways, taxa).

### `NodeEntity`

Abstract `bn:NodeEntity`: a pool of molecules or complexes acting as a node in pathway models.

### `EdgeEntity`

Abstract `bn:EdgeEntity`: a typed relationship with `left` and `right` participants.

### `Taxon`

Organism at species or genus level (`bn:Taxon`). Use `name` for the scientific name.

### `Provenance`

Provenance metadata (`bn:Provenance`); attached to entities via their `provenance` field.

### `Gene`

A gene (`bn:Gene`).

### `Dna`

A DNA element (`bn:Dna`).

### `Rna`

An RNA element (`bn:Rna`).

### `Protein`

A protein (`bn:Protein`).

### `MolecularComplex`

A biomolecular complex (`bn:Complex`).

### `SmallMolecule`

A small molecule (`bn:SmallMolecule`).

### `OrthologGroup`

A protein ortholog group (`bn:OrthologGroup`).

### `Interaction`

A physical/functional interaction between node entities (`bn:Interaction`).

### `Influence`

A directed influence whose target may be a node, an edge or a pathway (`bn:Influence`).

### `Reaction`

A biochemical reaction transforming left (substrates) into right (products) (`bn:Reaction`).

### `PathwayModule`

A pathway module grouping nodes, edges and sub-pathways (`bn:PathwayModule`).

### `class_name`

```
class_name(x) -> String
```

Local name of the ontology class of a resource or type (e.g. `"Complex"` for `MolecularComplex`).

### `Prop`

```
Prop(field, pred, kind, range)
```

Mapping of a struct field to a `bn:` predicate. `kind` is one of

  * `:ref`     – identifier of another resource in the graph; `range` is a tuple of allowed types
  * `:term`    – controlled-vocabulary `Symbol`; `range` is the root term it must descend from
  * `:iri`     – external IRI or CURIE (not resolved in the graph); `range` is `nothing`
  * `:literal` – data value; `range` is the XSD datatype local name

### `schema`

```
schema(T) -> Vector{Prop}
```

Field-to-predicate mapping for a resource type.

### `assign!`

```
assign!(r, field, value)
```

Set `field` of resource `r` from a plain value (string, number, vector), converting to the field's type. Vector fields accept a vector or a single value; `nothing` clears.


## Any format

### `load`

```
load(path; format = <from extension>, kwargs...) -> KnowledgeGraph
```

Read a graph from any supported format (see `formats()`). Keyword arguments go to the format's reader, e.g. `load("ppi.sif"; relationships = Dict("pp" => :Binding))` or `load("genes.csv"; type = Gene, mapping = Dict("symbol" => :name))`.

### `load!`

```
load!(kg, path; replace = false, kwargs...) -> kg
```

Load a file and merge it into `kg`. Tables and SIF are read straight into `kg`, so their rows can refer to (and update) resources already in it.

### `save`

```
save(path, kg; format = <from extension>, kwargs...) -> path
```

Write a graph in any supported format (see `formats()`); keyword arguments go to the writer, e.g. `save("edges.tsv", kg; types = EdgeEntity)` or `save("net.graphml", kg; reify = true)`.

### `formats`

```
formats() -> Vector of (format, extensions, read, write)
```

Supported file formats.


## RDF

### `IRI`

An RDF IRI (or a blank node written `_:label`).

### `Literal`

An RDF literal with an optional datatype IRI or language tag.

### `Triple`

An RDF triple.

### `triples`

```
triples(kg; inverses = true) -> Vector{Triple}
```

The graph as RDF triples. With `inverses = true`, inverse properties that are stored only one way (e.g. `bn:hasVariant`, `bn:participatesInPathway`, `bn:participatesInEdge`) are materialized as well.

### `from_triples`

```
from_triples(triples; base = BNR, prefixes = Dict()) -> KnowledgeGraph
```

Build a graph from RDF triples. Subjects typed with a concrete BioNExt class become resources; `bn:` predicates are mapped back through the schema (inverse and sub-properties are folded into their canonical field). Other triples are ignored. IRIs in a legacy BioNExt namespace are upgraded to the current one.

### `expand`

```
expand(kg, id) -> String
```

IRI for an identifier: full IRIs pass through, CURIEs with a known prefix are expanded (unknown prefixes go to identifiers.org), bare names are minted under `kg.base`.

### `compact`

```
compact(kg, iri) -> String
```

Inverse of `expand`.

### `write_turtle`

```
write_turtle(io_or_path, kg; inverses = true)
```

Serialize the graph as Turtle, grouped by subject.

### `parse_turtle`

```
parse_turtle(io_or_path; base = "") -> (triples, prefixes)
```

Parse a Turtle document into triples. Also returns the declared prefix map.

### `read_turtle`

```
read_turtle(io_or_path; base = nothing, prefixes = Dict()) -> KnowledgeGraph
```

### `write_ntriples`

```
write_ntriples(io_or_path, kg; inverses = true)
```

Serialize the graph as N-Triples (one triple per line, full IRIs).

### `parse_ntriples`

```
parse_ntriples(io_or_path) -> Vector{Triple}
```

### `read_ntriples`

```
read_ntriples(io_or_path; base = BNR, prefixes = Dict()) -> KnowledgeGraph
```

### `write_jsonld`

```
write_jsonld(io_or_path, kg; inverses = true)
```

Compact JSON-LD with an `@context` of the graph's prefixes and an `@graph` array.

### `parse_jsonld`

```
parse_jsonld(io_or_path) -> (triples, prefixes)
```

Read JSON-LD in compacted or expanded form: `@context` with prefix/term definitions (string or `{"@id", "@type": "@id"}`), `@graph`, `@id`, `@type`, value objects, node references and nested node objects. Remote contexts are not fetched.

### `read_jsonld`

```
read_jsonld(io_or_path; base = nothing, prefixes = Dict()) -> KnowledgeGraph
```

### `write_rdfxml`

```
write_rdfxml(io_or_path, kg; inverses = true)
```

Serialize the graph as RDF/XML (readable by Protégé, rdflib, Jena, ...).


## JSON and tables

### `write_json`

```
write_json(io_or_path, kg)
```

Plain JSON document: `{"format": "bionext-json", "base", "prefixes", "resources": [...]}`, one object per resource with `"class"`, `"id"` and every non-empty field by its Julia name.

### `read_json`

```
read_json(io_or_path) -> KnowledgeGraph
```

### `parse_json`

```
parse_json(io_or_string) -> Any
```

### `write_table`

```
write_table(io_or_path, kg; delim = '\t', types = Resource, list_sep = "|")
```

One row per resource of type `types` (e.g. `types = EdgeEntity` for an edge list). Columns: `class`, `id`, then every field used by those types.

### `read_table`

```
read_table(io_or_path; delim = '\t', type = nothing, mapping = Dict(), list_sep = "|", into = nothing)
```

Import a delimited table. Each row becomes (or updates) one resource.

  * the class comes from a `class` column, or from `type` (e.g. `type = Protein`)
  * `mapping` renames columns to fields, e.g. `Dict("Gene symbol" => :name, "source" => :left)`; other columns are matched to fields by name, and unknown columns are ignored
  * rows without an `id` column get generated ids (`protein-1`, ...)
  * rows whose id already exists with the same class update that resource
  * `into` adds to an existing graph instead of a new one


## Networks

### `Arc`

One arc of a flattened network; `role` is `:pair`, `:left` or `:right`.

### `network`

```
network(kg; reify = false, type = nothing) -> (nodes = Vector{String}, arcs = Vector{Arc})
```

Flatten the graph to a simple directed network (see `reify` above). Nodes are all node entities plus anything that appears as an arc endpoint. `type` keeps only edges whose relationship type `is_a` that term.

### `write_sif`

```
write_sif(io_or_path, kg; reify = false)
```

Simple Interaction Format: `source<TAB>relationship<TAB>target`, isolated nodes on their own line.

### `read_sif`

```
read_sif(io_or_path; node_type = Protein, edge_type = Interaction,
         relationships = Dict(), into = nothing) -> KnowledgeGraph
```

Import a SIF file (`source rel target1 target2 ...`, tab- or space-separated). Unknown nodes are created as `node_type`, each arc becomes an `edge_type` edge. Relationship names are matched to vocabulary terms by id or label, case-insensitively (`"activation"` → `:Activation`); `relationships` overrides, e.g. `Dict("pp" => :Binding)`.

### `write_graphml`

```
write_graphml(io_or_path, kg; reify = false)
```

GraphML for Cytoscape, Gephi, yEd or Graphs.jl. Node attributes: `class`, `name`; edge attributes: `type`, `edge_id`, `class`, `role`, `weight`, `confidence`.

### `write_dot`

```
write_dot(io_or_path, kg; reify = false)
```

Graphviz DOT; render with e.g. `dot -Tsvg graph.dot -o graph.svg`.
